takeoff_ground_roll_provenance.title: Short Field Takeoff Distance
takeoff_ground_roll_provenance.conditions: Flaps 20 deg; 2500 RPM, 39 in.hg. and mixture set at 34 GPH prior to brake release; cowl flaps open; paved, level, dry runway; zero wind
handbook_notes: Short field technique as specified in Section 4.
Decrease distances 10% for each 10 knots headwind. For operation with tail winds up to 10 knots, increase distances by 10% for each 2.5 knots.
For operation on dry, grass runway, increase distances by 15% of the “ground roll” figure.
takeoff_ground_roll_provenance.note: Lift off and speed at 50 feet as printed per sheet: 64 and 74 KIAS at 3600 lb, 61 and 71 KIAS at 3300 lb, 57 and 67 KIAS at 3000 lb. Three sheets, one per weight, PDF pages 170-172, read from the text layer. Every cell printed; no blanks. All 270 cells proven by eye against the rendered pages (backlog/evidence/FD-714/takeover/t206h/proof_takeoff.py). The Section 5 sample problem (page 5-5) prints 1310 ft ground roll and 2430 ft total at 3600 lb, 4000 ft, 30 C, which is the 4000 ft / 30 C cell of sheet 1.

landing_ground_roll_provenance.title: Short Field Landing Distance
landing_ground_roll_provenance.conditions: Flaps FULL; power idle; maximum braking; paved, level, dry runway; zero wind
handbook_notes: Short field technique as specified in Section 4.
Decrease distances 10% for each 10 knots headwind. For operation with tail winds up to 10 knots, increase distances by 10% for each 2.5 knots.
For operation on dry grass runway, increase distances by 40% of the “ground roll” figure.
If landing with Flaps UP, increase the approach speed by 9 KIAS and allow for 45% longer distances.
landing_ground_roll_provenance.note: Speed at 50 Feet: 64 KIAS (conditions block). One sheet at 3600 lb, PDF page 194, read from the text layer. Every cell printed. One handbook misprint (1000 ft / 30 C total distance printed 1790, where its own row and column imply about 1530) is published AS PRINTED: it is the more conservative figure (operator ruling 2026-09-28), see disputed_cells. All 90 cells proven by eye (backlog/evidence/FD-714/takeover/t206h/proof_landing.py). The sample problem (page 5-9) prints 865 ft and 1580 ft at 3000 ft / 30 C, the 3000 ft / 30 C cell.

handbook_misprints_kept.method: printed value kept: it is already the more conservative of the two (longer than or equal to the 40 C cell's 1530)
handbook_misprints_kept.reason: Figure 5-12 (page 5-40) prints 1790 ft total distance at 1000 ft / 30 C. Its own row reads 1450 at 20 C and 1530 at 40 C, and its own column reads 1450 at sea level and 1530 at 2000 ft, so 1790 breaks the rise with both temperature and altitude. The same misprint is in the 206H book (specs/c206h.json). The printed 1790 is the longer, more conservative figure, so it is published as printed (operator ruling 2026-09-28: a distance takes max(printed, bound)); the 40 C cell's 1530 is logged beside it in handbook_misprints_kept. Nothing is computed.
